Class RoleAssignmentService

java.lang.Object
edu.ucsb.cs.taapply.services.RoleAssignmentService
@Service public class RoleAssignmentService extends Object
The single place that decides which roles an email address holds.

This is deliberately shared by GoogleSignInServiceImpl (at login) and RoleUpdateInterceptor (on every request). Those two must always agree, and they previously held separate copies of the logic, which is a drift risk that grows with each new role.

There are three roles. ADMIN and INSTRUCTOR are independent: a user may hold either, both or neither. USER is held by everyone who is signed in. A user with nothing but USER is an applicant: a UCSB student who may apply to any open TA or ULA recruitment.

    • MANAGED_ROLES

      public static final Set<String> MANAGED_ROLES
      The roles this service owns. The interceptor strips these before recomputing, so that a role removed from the database is dropped from a live session too.

    • ACCESS_ROLES

      public static final Set<String> ACCESS_ROLES
      Holding one of these entitles someone to use the app whatever their address. ROLE_USER is not among them: it is granted to anyone who can complete a Google login, which is not a decision this app makes.

  • Method Details

    • grantsAccess

      public static boolean grantsAccess(String email, Collection<? extends org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authorities)
      Whether this user may use the app: anyone with a UCSB address, who is then at least an applicant, and anyone in the admin or instructor tables whatever their address. A signed-in Google user with an outside address who is in neither table has only ROLE_USER, and is turned away.

    • isUcsbEmail

      public static boolean isUcsbEmail(String email)
      Whether an address belongs to UCSB. The address is canonicalized first, so @umail.ucsb.edu counts (CanonicalFormConverter maps it to @ucsb.edu) and case does not matter.

    • authoritiesFor

      public Set<org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authoritiesFor(String email)
      Every authority the given email should hold. ROLE_USER is always granted: there is no role hierarchy, so without it an admin would fail hasRole('ROLE_USER').
